Craft Anything

English · 日本語 · 简体中文 · 한국어

See how any website, app or game works, then have AI build your own version; an open-source, clean-room engine in pure Rust.
Point it at a target, say what you want, and it studies the original with real inspection tools,
has a coding agent build a new project, checks the result against the original and refines it.

Download Craft Anything · ArtCraft · All Crafting Apps



A website project: each check says how alike the build is, you approve anything outside the rules, and the plan shows what's left.

> [!NOTE] > **ArtCraft is a community of artists from all walks of life.** Painters, photographers, > filmmakers, illustrators, designers, animators, hobbyists, and people who picked up a pencil > last week. If you make things, you're one of us. **[Come say hi on Discord](https://discord.gg/artcraft).**

How it works · Two ways to use it · AI · Agents · Under the hood · Get started · Status · Downloads · Discord


🔍 Study anything

Websites, desktop apps, phone apps, games and files: real inspection tools find out how they're built and what they do, with the evidence behind every answer.

🛠️ Build your own

Say what you want ("Recreate this website", "Recreate this game's gameplay in Rust") and a coding agent builds a new project in the stack you ask for.

✅ Checked, not guessed

Every build is compared with the original (pages at three screen widths, a game's own self-test, an app's runs) and refined until it's close.

🤖 Agent-ready

320 tools, each one a CLI command and an MCP tool, so any agent can drive the same engine the app uses. No AI is needed to inspect.

## How it works Point Craft Anything at a target, say what you want, and press Start. It works in four steps, asking you in plain words when a decision is yours: 1. **Study:** inspect the original: its pages at every width, its code, its files, how it runs. 2. **Build:** a coding agent builds a new project, in the language, framework or engine your request names (or a sensible default). 3. **Check:** compare the build with the original and list what doesn't match yet. 4. **Ready:** open, play or preview the result, or ask for changes and it refines it.

Make: pick what to recreate, say what you want, press Start.
Ready: play the game, or ask for changes below.
## Two ways to use it - **Simple** (default): "What do you want to make?" Pick a website, app or game, describe it, press Start. A project page shows the four steps (Study → Build → Check → Ready), what the agent is doing in plain words, question and approval cards, how alike the result is, and buttons to open the result or its folder. Ask for changes in the box at the bottom. "Just look inside" opens a target for questions without building anything (in Deep mode). - **Advanced**: the full workbench: every tool (Ctrl/Cmd+K), functions, strings, pseudo-C, disassembly, hex, call graphs, evidence, unknowns, jobs, logs and the agent console. Both modes drive the same engine. ## Clean room or Deep - **Clean room** (the default): nothing inside the original is read, not its code, files or page source. Craft Anything works from what you can see: pictures you add, the website as a visitor sees it (screenshots, visible text, measured layout, colours, fonts and spacing, menus opened) and, when you allow it, a picture of the app's window. Tools that would look inside are refused and say how to turn on Deep mode. - **Deep**: every tool is used, for your private use. A program's code and files are read with the built-in engines (and Ghidra when it's installed), a website's JavaScript is read and its start page watched, and the builder may use all of them. Clean room is a rule about what Craft Anything offers and refuses. It is not an operating-system sandbox: it doesn't isolate your computer. A coding agent you run still acts as you, and what it can read, write or run depends on its own permissions. Which of an agent's own tools Craft Anything can refuse differs by agent; for Claude Code's tools in chats and questions, see [`docs/claude-code.md`](docs/claude-code.md). Switch in the title bar or Settings, with `settings_set deep_mode true`, or for one CLI run with `--deep` (or `--clean-room`).


Advanced: functions, pseudo-C, the agent and the evidence behind every answer.

## AI Building needs a coding agent on your computer. **Claude Code** is supported first: Craft Anything runs your own, unmodified `claude` program, which uses your own sign-in; Craft Anything never sees or handles your account. Your use of it falls under your own agreement with Anthropic. See [docs/claude-code.md](docs/claude-code.md) for how and why. A Codex adapter exists but hasn't been verified on a real install yet. **GitHub Copilot** can use your installed Copilot CLI through ACP: sign in separately with `copilot login`. Other agents that speak ACP (Gemini CLI, Qwen Code, opencode, goose, Hermes, Maki) can be switched to it per backend; of those, only Maki has been run live. Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter and local OpenAI-compatible servers are available for questions and analysis (Settings → AI). ## Built for agents Every tool is also a CLI subcommand and an MCP tool, so an agent can study a target or run a whole rebuild without the app: ```sh craft-anything-cli commands # every tool, by toolset craft-anything-cli mcp # serve them to any MCP client craft-anything-cli rebuild https://example.com "Recreate this website" ``` Results are evidence records with their confidence, coverage and limitations; big ones come back as a summary first and are paged with `core_evidence_browse`. `craft-anything-cli setup` connects Craft Anything to coding-agent apps. ## Under the hood A pure-Rust reverse-engineering engine with 320 tools (300 in the engine, the rest from the AI and setup layers) for native programs, .NET, Java, Android, Apple, Electron/JavaScript, websites, firmware, packet captures, databases and game files. Its own decoders, disassembler and decompiler work without any outside program; Deep mode uses them all, and Ghidra when it's installed. It powers the desktop app (egui), the CLI and the MCP server, and parts of it run in the browser as WebAssembly. The full list is in [docs/tools.md](docs/tools.md). ## Get started Requires Rust **1.97 or newer** (a dependency needs it; `rustup update`). On Debian or Ubuntu, the desktop app also needs: ```sh sudo apt-get install libxkbcommon-dev libwayland-dev libx11-dev libxrandr-dev libxi-dev libgl1-mesa-dev libgtk-3-dev ``` Then: ```sh git clone https://github.com/storytold/craft-anything && cd craft-anything cargo run --release -p craft-anything # the desktop app cargo install --path apps/craft-anything-cli # the CLI, as `craft-anything-cli` craft-anything-cli doctor # checks the install, coding agents and engines ``` Building needs a coding agent signed in on your computer (see [AI](#ai)); `doctor` says what's missing. Rebuild from the command line (questions are asked in the terminal): ```sh craft-anything-cli rebuild https://example.com "Recreate this website" craft-anything-cli rebuild - "A snake game in Rust" --rounds 1 craft-anything-cli rebuild https://example.com "Make the header blue" --continue-in "" craft-anything-cli rebuild - "Add a contact form" --project-folder "" --existing edit ``` New projects go in `Documents/Craft Anything` (change it in Settings → General). Each project folder holds `craft.json` (the request, target, status and history), `capture/` (what was recorded from the target), `app/` (the generated project), `checks/` (each comparison against the original), `investigation.cany/` (evidence) and `inbox/` (open questions). A project can also start in a folder you pick (Choose a folder… under Start, or `--project-folder`). If it already has files, you say what they are: the app itself, which the builder edits in place, or material to start from, with the app built in `app/` beside them (Settings → General can remember the answer). Settings → General also lists projects from more folders; removing one only takes it off the list. ## Status > [!IMPORTANT] > **Status:** Craft Anything is in early alpha. What works today, what is partial and what's next: > > - **Works today:** the desktop app (Simple and Advanced), the CLI and the MCP server; the > Study → Build → Check → Refine workflow for websites, apps and games with Claude Code as the > builder; website checks at three screen widths; game rebuilds in Unity, Unreal or Godot; Deep > mode with Ghidra; generated pictures and 3D models (opt-in, your own fal.ai key); plugins (MCP > servers, and WASM components in builds with the `wasm-plugins` option). > - **Partly there:** building with API keys and other coding agents (built, not yet run live), > behaviour checks for apps and games, a few engine tools tested only against stand-ins. > - **Released:** public releases with installers for Windows, macOS, Linux and FreeBSD are > published on the [Releases page](https://github.com/storytold/craft-anything/releases); they are > still alpha. > - **Next:** the managed tier. > > [docs/STATUS.md](docs/STATUS.md) has the detail and how each part was checked, > [docs/tool-status.md](docs/tool-status.md) the tool-by-tool checklist, and > [docs/ROADMAP.md](docs/ROADMAP.md) the plan, item by item. Please file issues, or tell us what > broke on [Discord](https://discord.gg/artcraft). **Responsible use.** Use Craft Anything on software you own or are allowed to examine. It never bypasses DRM, logins or anti-cheat. Rebuilds recreate layout, style and behaviour from evidence; the agent is told not to copy logos, photos or text unless you confirm you own them or have permission. **Installing dependencies runs code.** When a builder installs a project's dependencies, the commands run on your computer, and the packages can run code while they install. npm runs each package's install scripts by default, and Rust build scripts and Python source packages run their own setup code. Craft Anything asks before a command of a kind it hasn't seen in this project (`npm`, `cargo`…). Choosing "always allow" for `npm` lets every later npm command run without asking, so only do that for a project whose dependencies you trust. To install npm packages without their install scripts, run `npm install --ignore-scripts`. ## Downloads On GitHub, the [latest release](https://github.com/storytold/craft-anything/releases/latest) has every build listed below, and [all releases](https://github.com/storytold/craft-anything/releases) has earlier versions and their notes. `` in the file names is the version number, and `SHA256SUMS.txt` lists a checksum for every file. ### Windows | Build | Installer | Portable | |---|---|---| | x64 (64-bit Intel/AMD) | `craft-anything--windows-x64.msi` | `craft-anything--windows-x64-portable.zip` | | arm64 (Snapdragon and other ARM PCs) | `craft-anything--windows-arm64.msi` | `craft-anything--windows-arm64-portable.zip` | | x86 (32-bit) | `craft-anything--windows-x86.msi` | `craft-anything--windows-x86-portable.zip` | Installers and executables are code-signed. The portable zip keeps its settings next to the app. ### macOS | Build | File | Notes | |---|---|---| | App, universal (Apple silicon + Intel) | `craft-anything--macos-universal.dmg` | Signed and notarized | | Command-line tool, universal | `craft-anything-cli--macos-universal.zip` | Signed and notarized; see below if macOS blocks it | Versions after 0.2.0 include the command-line tool in the app, so builds don't need the separate zip. You only need it to use the command line without the app. A browser download of the zip can stop with "Apple could not verify craft-anything-cli" (a lone program can't carry its notarization with it, so macOS has to look it up online). A download from the terminal isn't checked this way, so use this instead: ```sh ver=0.2.0 # change this to the version you want curl -fLO "https://github.com/storytold/craft-anything/releases/download/v$ver/craft-anything-cli-$ver-macos-universal.zip" ditto -x -k "craft-anything-cli-$ver-macos-universal.zip" . mkdir -p ~/.local/bin mv "craft-anything-cli-$ver-macos-universal/craft-anything-cli" ~/.local/bin/ ~/.local/bin/craft-anything-cli --version ``` To run it as just `craft-anything-cli`, add `~/.local/bin` to your `PATH`. If you already have the blocked copy, press Done (not Move to Bin), then run `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine `, or allow it in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway. #### Checking that a Mac download is signed and notarized Each Mac release is signed with a Developer ID certificate and notarized by Apple. To check a download yourself, run these in Terminal (replace `` with the version and the paths with yours): ```sh # The disk image: "accepted" and "source=Notarized Developer ID" mean it passed spctl --assess --type open --context context:primary-signature -v "craft-anything--macos-universal.dmg" # The notarization ticket is attached: prints "The validate action worked!" xcrun stapler validate "craft-anything--macos-universal.dmg" # The app, after you open the disk image: the signature must verify codesign --verify --deep --strict --verbose=2 "/Volumes//Craft Anything.app" spctl --assess --type execute --verbose "/Volumes//Craft Anything.app" # The command-line tool: a bare program can't carry a ticket, so macOS checks it online codesign --verify --strict --verbose=2 ~/.local/bin/craft-anything-cli codesign -dv --verbose=4 ~/.local/bin/craft-anything-cli 2>&1 | grep Authority ``` The `Authority` lines should name a "Developer ID Application" certificate. If a check fails, don't run the file; report it with the output and the release tag. ### Linux | Format | x86_64 | aarch64 (ARM64) | Notes | |---|---|---|---| | AppImage | `craft-anything--linux-x86_64.AppImage` | `craft-anything--linux-aarch64.AppImage` | Runs anywhere; updates itself with [AppImageUpdate](https://github.com/AppImageCommunity/AppImageUpdate) (`.zsync` files) | | Flatpak | `craft-anything--linux-x86_64.flatpak` | `craft-anything--linux-aarch64.flatpak` | Sandboxed; `flatpak install --user ` | | Debian/Ubuntu | `craft-anything--linux-x86_64.deb` | `craft-anything--linux-aarch64.deb` | | | Fedora/RHEL/openSUSE | `craft-anything--linux-x86_64.rpm` | `craft-anything--linux-aarch64.rpm` | | | Tarball | `craft-anything--linux-x86_64.tar.gz` | `craft-anything--linux-aarch64.tar.gz` | Unpack anywhere | RISC-V (riscv64): `craft-anything--linux-riscv64.tar.gz`, a tarball only. The AppImage carries the CLI too: run ` --cli ` (for example ` --cli mcp` for an MCP client), or make a link to the AppImage named `craft-anything-cli` and run that. ### FreeBSD | Build | File | |---|---| | x86_64 | `craft-anything--freebsd-x86_64.tar.gz` | ### Web (WebAssembly) | Build | File | Notes | |---|---|---| | Browser viewer | `craft-anything-web-.zip` | Says what a file is, in the browser (the file never leaves it); host the folder on any static web server ([packaging/web/README.md](packaging/web/README.md)) |

items.description: Auto Ontology is a Python framework for building semantic, graph-based reasoning layers over data. It enables deterministic query generation, better context retrieval, and more explainable AI for LLM and agent workflows.
items.readme_text:
# Auto Ontology Agents can retrieve documents and query databases, but reliability gates agentic analytics: a revenue metric answered faster is worth nothing if the number is wrong. Agents need a context layer that tells them where data lives, what it means, whether to use it, how to use it, where it came from, and what is similar. NVIDIA Auto Ontology is an open library that builds that layer from enterprise metadata, reconciles definitions across systems, and exposes it to any agent harness through MCP, CLI, and API. It complements the semantic models customers already own. It enables developers to: - Discover: generate enterprise ontologies from metadata; connect existing ontologies and semantic models; build AI-ready knowledge graphs. - Ground: give agents trusted business meaning for metrics, entities, and relationships; reconcile inconsistent definitions across systems. - Validate: check generated queries against certified definitions and lineage; return provenance with every answer. - Expose: serve context to any agent harness through MCP, CLI, and API. Learn: fold certified corrections and usage back into the ontology, so shared context improves with every question. ## Benchmarks To run a text-to-SQL benchmark such as BIRD, refer to the [ontology SQL evaluation repository](https://github.com/NVIDIA/ontology-sql-eval/). > **Licensing & contributions.** Auto Ontology is distributed under the > [Apache License 2.0](./LICENSE). Third-party open-source components > bundled, linked, or otherwise used by this project are listed in > [`THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`](./THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). **This project > is currently not accepting external contributions.**

## Key Features - **Natural-language querying** of structured data — questions are translated to SQL and executed against connected databases, powered by NVIDIA NIM. - **Semantic catalog / ontology layer** over relational sources, stored in Postgres alongside the catalog it describes. - **Authentication & RBAC** —using [Better Auth](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth). - **Web UI** for chat, analysis, data catalog, analytics, and settings. - **Flexible deployment** — Helm chart for Kubernetes or Docker Compose for a local stack. ## Software Components | Component | Technology | Role | Default port | | ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ------------ | | Frontend | Next.js 16 (React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS 4), Better Auth, Prisma | Web UI, authentication, API gateway | 3000 | | Backend | FastAPI (Python 3.12+), LangChain | Chat / NL-to-SQL, catalog, datasource APIs | 3001 | | Ingestion worker | FastAPI (Python 3.12+) | Ingests tabular data and writes embeddings | 3002 | | Postgres + pgvector | Relational Database | App metadata, the catalog and ontology, vector store | 5432 | | HashiCorp Vault | Optional | Secure storage of connection credentials | — | ### NVIDIA NIM Auto Ontology uses NVIDIA NIM endpoints for inference — either the hosted [NVIDIA API catalog](https://build.nvidia.com) (`integrate.api.nvidia.com`) or self-hosted NIMs. The defaults in `.env.example` are: - **LLM:** `nvidia/nemotron-3.5-lightning-30b-a3b` - **Embeddings:** `nvidia/nemotron-3-embed-1b` - **Reranking:** `nvidia/llama-nemotron-rerank-vl-1b-v2` The endpoints and models are configured via the `DEFAULT_MODELS_ENDPOINT`, `DEFAULT_MODELS_MODEL`, `EMBED_ENDPOINT`, and `EMBED_MODEL` environment variables and require a `DEFAULT_MODELS_API_KEY`. #### Model triplets Each model role is configured by a **triplet** of environment variables — `_ENDPOINT` (URL), `_API_KEY`, and `_MODEL`: | Prefix | Role | | ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | | `DEFAULT_MODELS` | Shared default; every field below falls back to it. | | `REASONING` | Main chat / NL-to-SQL model. | | `NON_REASONING` | Lighter model used for entity extraction. | | `EMBED` | Text-embedding model (must match between ingest and query). | | `RERANK` | Reranker used by the retrieval flow. | You can set a full triplet, only some of its fields, or none at all — any field left unset falls back to the matching `DEFAULT_MODELS_`. So the simplest setup is to fill in `DEFAULT_MODELS_*` and override per-triplet fields only where they differ (e.g. `EMBED_MODEL`, `NON_REASONING_MODEL`). `*_API_KEY` also falls back to the legacy `NVIDIA_API_KEY` for backward compatibility. ## Quickstart This runs Auto-Ontology with Docker Compose against Wide World Importers, Microsoft's sample sales database. You need Docker with Compose v2, [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), and an NVIDIA API key (`nvapi-...`) from [build.nvidia.com](https://build.nvidia.com). 1. Clone the repository and create `.env`: ```bash git clone https://github.com/NVIDIA/auto-ontology.git && cd auto-ontology cp .env.example .env ``` Then set these values in `.env`: ```dotenv DEFAULT_MODELS_API_KEY=nvapi-... AUTH_SECRET= APP_URL=http://localhost:3000 POSTGRES_PASSWORD= CONNECTION_STRINGS=postgresql://postgres:@postgres:5432/wideworldimporters AUTO_ONTOLOGY_ADMIN_PASSWORD= PGADMIN_PASSWORD= ``` Compose publishes Postgres, pgAdmin, and the web app on the host, so replace each default password before you start it. `.env.example` also sets an API key per model role: replace each `nvapi-your-api-key-here` with your key, or delete those lines so they fall back to `DEFAULT_MODELS_API_KEY`. 2. Start Postgres and load the sample database. The seed script lives in auto-ontology-eval; pass it the Postgres password you set: ```bash docker compose up -d --wait postgres git clone https://github.com/NVIDIA/auto-ontology-eval.git ../auto-ontology-eval (cd ../auto-ontology-eval && uv sync && cp .env.example .env && \ POSTGRES_PASSWORD='' \ uv run python scripts/seed/seed_wwi.py --database-name wideworldimporters --drop) ``` 3. Build and start the rest of the stack: ```bash docker compose up -d --build ``` 4. Open and sign in with `AUTO_ONTOLOGY_ADMIN_EMAIL` and `AUTO_ONTOLOGY_ADMIN_PASSWORD` from `.env`. Go to **Settings → Semantic Compilation** and turn it on. Ingestion runs at startup; compilation starts immediately and reports **Semantic compilation is ready** when it finishes. 5. Ask a question in **Chat**: > What was revenue for the USB food flash drive - sushi roll in Pennsylvania > in June 2015? The agent resolves *revenue*, *product*, and *state* to terms in the ontology, follows their relationships to the joins it needs, and runs the query. The answer comes back with its SQL and the steps that produced it, so you can check the result against the source: ```text Answer: Revenue for USB food flash drive - sushi roll in Pennsylvania in June 2015 was $588.80, from 3 invoice lines. SQL: SELECT SUM(il.extendedprice) AS revenue, COUNT(*) AS invoice_lines FROM sales.invoicelines il JOIN sales.invoices i ON il.invoiceid = i.invoiceid JOIN warehouse.stockitems si ON il.stockitemid = si.stockitemid JOIN sales.customers c ON i.customerid = c.customerid JOIN application.cities ct ON c.deliverycityid = ct.cityid JOIN application.stateprovinces sp ON ct.stateprovinceid = sp.stateprovinceid WHERE si.stockitemname = 'USB food flash drive - sushi roll' AND sp.stateprovincename = 'Pennsylvania' AND i.invoicedate >= '2015-06-01' AND i.invoicedate < '2015-07-01' Steps: Resolved terms: Invoice Line (revenue), Stock Item, State Province, Invoice Joined: invoice line -> invoice -> customer -> city -> state province Validated the filter values against the data, then executed ``` 6. Ask something the data can't answer. Wide World Importers has no advertising data, so a question about ad spend has nothing to resolve against. An agent connected through [MCP](#mcp-server) checks answerability first and asks you to clarify: ```text You: What was return on ad spend for the sushi roll flash drive in June 2015? Agent: check_answerable -> coverage 0.5; no term covers "ad spend" Agent: I can find revenue for that product, but this data has no advertising spend, so I can't compute return on ad spend. Do you want June 2015 revenue instead, or is ad spend tracked in another source I should connect? ``` If the UI loads without its left navigation after a restart, the browser is holding a stale session cookie. Clear site data for `localhost:3000` and sign in again. For other setup failures, see the [setup skill's troubleshooting guide](./skills/nvidia-ontology-setup/references/troubleshooting.md). ## How it works

Auto-Ontology works in three stages: it generates an ontology, people certify it, and the agent answers questions from it. The ontology holds three kinds of definition: - **Terms.** Business concepts such as *Customer* or *Invoice Line*, each with a description and synonyms, mapped to the columns that hold them. - **SQL attributes.** Reviewed SQL expressions under a term, such as a margin or a rolling total. The agent reuses them, so answers compute each measure the same way. - **Relationships.** How tables join, including bridge tables, inferred from keys and from the data. **Generate.** The ingestion service builds a first draft from the source databases: 1. Read sources: extract schemas, profile columns, and sample values into the catalog. 2. Name entities: extract terms table by table and map each to columns. 3. Resolve relationships: infer joins between tables and bridge tables, and suggest SQL attributes from query history. 4. Write the ontology: store terms, relationships, and SQL attributes in Postgres, with embeddings in pgvector for retrieval. The result is a semantic graph you can explore in the UI. In this example, one compilation of Wide World Importers produced 31 terms; selecting **Order** shows its description, related terms, mapped columns, and SQL attributes:

**Certify.** People make the draft trustworthy: 1. Test with real questions in Chat, or with `check_answerable` and `ask_question` over MCP. 2. Refine terms, descriptions, and SQL attributes in the UI or through the API. 3. Certify names, descriptions, and SQL attributes once they're correct. **Answer.** For each question, the agent: 1. Classifies the intent and extracts the entities the question names. 2. Retrieves candidate terms, columns, and SQL attributes by embedding search. 3. Writes SQL from those candidates. 4. Checks the filter values and the query against the database, repairing the SQL when a check fails. 5. Runs the query and returns the answer with its SQL and the steps it took. When the candidates can't support a query, the agent reports that the question can't be answered from this data. Predictive questions go to KumoRFM when it's configured (see [Predictions](#predictions)). In Chat, each answer shows its SQL, and you can view the rows, download them as CSV, or read them as a chart:

Auto-Ontology is compatible with [Apache Ossie](https://ossie.apache.org/), the open standard for exchanging semantic models. Ossie includes a [converter for Auto-Ontology](https://github.com/apache/ossie-converters/tree/main/nvidia), which Auto-Ontology uses to import and export model definitions as Ossie YAML. Use **Settings → Import / Export**, or `POST /api/model/import` and `POST /api/model/export`. | Component | Technology | Role | Port | | ------------------- | --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ---- | | Frontend | Next.js, Better Auth, Prisma | Web UI, authentication, public API gateway | 3000 | | Backend | FastAPI (Python 3.12+), LangChain | Text-to-SQL agent, catalog, ontology APIs | 3001 | | Ingestion service | FastAPI (Python 3.12+) | Ingestion and semantic compilation | 3002 | | MCP server | FastMCP | Read-only agent tools over the public API | 3003 | | Postgres + pgvector | PostgreSQL 17 | Catalog, ontology, app data, vector store | 5432 | | HashiCorp Vault | Optional | Connection credential storage | n/a | Keep ports 3001 and 3002 on a private network. FastAPI trusts the user identity the frontend forwards in the `x-auto-ontology-user-id` header, and the ingestion service's endpoints (ingest, delete, reset, compile) have no authentication of their own. Clients go through the web app on port 3000. ## Use it from your agent ### MCP server The [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server gives any MCP client read-only tools over the ontology. Each user signs in through Auto-Ontology, and every call runs with that user's permissions. | Job | Tools | | ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | | Readiness | `check_readiness`: can this deployment answer anything at all | | Terms | `search_terms`, `get_term`, `get_term_columns`, `get_term_sql_attributes`, `get_sql_attribute`, `describe_table` | | Answerability | `check_answerable`: does the ontology cover this question | | Questions | `ask_question`: the answer, the SQL, and the rows | Run the server against your deployment: ```bash AUTO_ONTOLOGY_API_URL=http://localhost:3000 \ uvx --from "git+https://github.com/NVIDIA/auto-ontology.git#subdirectory=mcp" auto-ontology-mcp ``` Cursor (`~/.cursor/mcp.json`): ```json { "mcpServers": { "auto-ontology": { "url": "http://localhost:3003/mcp" } } } ``` Claude Desktop (`claude_desktop_config.json`), bridged with [`mcp-remote`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/mcp-remote): ```json { "mcpServers": { "auto-ontology": { "command": "npx", "args": ["mcp-remote", "http://localhost:3003/mcp"] } } } ``` Restart the client after editing its config, then sign in when it prompts. Sign-in, configuration, and troubleshooting are in [docs/mcp.md](./docs/mcp.md). ### Agent skills Three skills teach a coding agent to work with Auto-Ontology. Start at [AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md). | Skill | Covers | | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | | [`nvidia-ontology-setup`](./skills/nvidia-ontology-setup/) | Install, connect sources, compile, prove readiness | | [`nvidia-ontology-management`](./skills/nvidia-ontology-management/) | Inspect, model, certify, import/export, and publish | | [`nvidia-ontology-query`](./skills/nvidia-ontology-query/) | Ask questions and validate the SQL, rows, and answer | ### REST API Ask a question with `POST /api/chat/completions` on the web app's origin. Mint an API token under the user menu → **API Tokens**. The response is a server-sent event stream: a `result` event carries the answer, and `data: [DONE]` ends the stream. ```bash curl -N http://localhost:3000/api/chat/completions \ -H "x-api-key: $AUTO_ONTOLOGY_API_TOKEN" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"question": "How many orders shipped last week?"}' ``` ```python import json import os import requests response = requests.post( "http://localhost:3000/api/chat/completions", headers={"x-api-key": os.environ["AUTO_ONTOLOGY_API_TOKEN"]}, json={"question": "How many orders shipped last week?"}, stream=True, timeout=900, ) response.raise_for_status() for line in response.iter_lines(decode_unicode=True): if not line or not line.startswith("data:"): continue payload = line.removeprefix("data:").strip() if payload == "[DONE]": break event = json.loads(payload) if event["type"] == "result": print(event["answer"]["response"]) print(event["answer"]["sql_code"]) elif event["type"] == "error": raise RuntimeError(event["message"]) ``` Event types, multi-turn conversations, and the gateway trust boundary are in [docs/conversation-api.md](./docs/conversation-api.md). Every other operation is in the [OpenAPI spec](./docs/openapi/auto-ontology-api.json). ## Connectors, models, and predictions ### Sources Auto-Ontology connects to ten engines: - PostgreSQL - MySQL - Databricks - Snowflake - ClickHouse - Trino - Apache Kyuubi - HeavyDB - DuckDB - SQLite Add connections under **Settings → Connections**, or list them in `CONNECTION_STRINGS`. DuckDB and SQLite are connection-string only. See [docs/connections.md](./docs/connections.md) for URL schemes, scoping, and credential storage. ### Models Auto-Ontology uses four model roles. With an `nvapi-` key, each defaults to an NVIDIA NIM on [build.nvidia.com](https://build.nvidia.com): | Role | Default model | What it does | | --------------- | --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | `REASONING` | `nvidia/nemotron-3.5-lightning-30b-a3b` | Builds the ontology (terms, relationships, SQL attributes), writes each answer's SQL and explanation, and grades answerability | | `NON_REASONING` | `nvidia/nemotron-3.5-lightning-30b-a3b` | Runs the agent's faster steps: question intent, entity extraction, candidate selection, and SQL checks and repair | | `EMBED` | `nvidia/nemotron-3.5-embed-1b` | Indexes tables, columns, terms, and SQL attributes in pgvector, and matches each question to them | | `RERANK` | `nvidia/nemotron-3.5-rerank-8b` | Ranks candidate tables when compilation builds bridge-table SQL attributes | To use self-hosted NIM or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, set `_ENDPOINT`, `_API_KEY`, and `_MODEL`. Any field you leave unset falls back to `DEFAULT_MODELS_`, so the simplest setup fills in `DEFAULT_MODELS_*` and overrides only what differs. Use models that support structured output, and keep the embedding model the same for ingestion and queries. [`.env.example`](./.env.example) documents every variable. ### Predictions Set `KUMO_RFM_API_KEY` and the agent routes predictive questions to KumoRFM. KumoRFM is a hosted service: to answer, the agent uploads the connected tables to it, capped by `KUMO_MAX_TABLES` (20 by default) and `KUMO_MAX_ROWS_PER_TABLE` (unlimited unless set). Review what that sends, and complete your organization's data review, before you enable it. ## Integrate with us To integrate an agent platform, application, or storage provider with Auto-Ontology, [open an integration request](https://github.com/NVIDIA/auto-ontology/issues/new?template=integration.yml). The Auto-Ontology team maintains the code and doesn't accept external pull requests. Integration requests and bug reports are welcome as issues. Report security vulnerabilities through [SECURITY.md](./SECURITY.md). Maintainer workflow is in [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md). ## Reference | Topic | Doc | | --------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | | Kubernetes deployment with Helm | [DEPLOYMENT.md](./DEPLOYMENT.md) | | Connections, scoping, and Vault | [docs/connections.md](./docs/connections.md) | | Authentication, SSO, and API tokens | [docs/authentication.md](./docs/authentication.md) | | Conversation API | [docs/conversation-api.md](./docs/conversation-api.md) | | MCP server | [docs/mcp.md](./docs/mcp.md) | | REST API | [docs/openapi/auto-ontology-api.json](./docs/openapi/auto-ontology-api.json) | ## License Auto-Ontology is licensed under the [Apache License, Version 2.0](./LICENSE). SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0 ``` Third-party open-source components used by Auto-Ontology are enumerated, with their upstream licenses and project URLs, in [`THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`](./THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). Components added by the container images are listed separately in [`CONTAINER_THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`](./CONTAINER_THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). ## Notice and Disclaimer NOTICE AND DISCLAIMER: This software automatically retrieves, accesses or interacts with external materials. --- See a feature in an app that you want in your own product? Ask your agent to investigate it with REA. It can inspect the app without its source code, explain how the feature works, show the evidence, and build a version for your project. REA connects your agent to tools for inspecting native binaries, JavaScript and Electron apps, .NET assemblies, and websites. You can also use the same tools from your terminal. Analysis runs locally, and results include the evidence and limitations behind each conclusion. Setup registers REA with your agent and installs matching workflow instructions. Native analysis can use an existing Hopper, Ghidra, IDA or Kuna installation; setup can optionally install Hopper with approval. Static JavaScript analysis needs no native analysis engine. > **[Visit the REA website](https://rea.tools/)** for setup instructions, illustrated guides, and real case studies. ## Quick start On Linux, Ghidra, JADX, firmware tool launches and static JavaScript/Electron analysis require a procps-compatible `ps` on REA's `PATH` for process ownership checks. Recovery steps are in `docs/installation.md` under "Linux owned-process prerequisite". ### Set up your agent With Node.js and npm installed, run: ```bash npx rea-agents setup ``` Choose your agents, review the proposed changes, and approve them. Setup adds REA's MCP server and matching workflow instructions, with backups of existing configuration. Restart your agent afterward. Setup records the selected runtime and REA entry script directly. If acquired through a package runner, keep its cache entry available. Run package acquisition from a trusted directory outside the target project. Installation and recovery details are in the setup guide below. Setup supports Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Grok Build and [other agents](docs/installation.md#supported-agents). See [installation and setup](docs/installation.md) for provider configuration and manual MCP registration and Claude Code/Codex plugin installation. MCP uses compact input schemas by default to reduce context overhead. Set `REA_MCP_INPUT_SCHEMA_PROFILE=full` in your MCP registration when you need the complete advertised field guidance and nested validation details. Both profiles keep the full tool set and canonical server validation. See "Compact input schema profile" in the MCP contracts guide. Complete output schemas are advertised by default. If your client caps the complete `tools/list` frame, set `REA_MCP_OUTPUT_SCHEMA_PROFILE=compact` to bound each advertised output schema, or `off` to omit output schemas entirely. Both settings keep canonical server-side validation and complete structured results. See "Output schemas" in the MCP contracts guide. ### Ask your agent ```text Understand how search works in the Notes app, show me the evidence, and build a similar feature for my project. ``` Replace Notes with your target app and the feature you want to understand. ### Use the terminal Inspect an extracted JavaScript/Electron app directory or ASAR: ```bash npx -y rea-agents@latest analyze-javascript-application /absolute/path/to/app --json ``` The result includes modules, imports, Electron boundaries and their evidence. Replace the path with your target, such as `"D:/apps/example"` on Windows. To install the `rea` command for regular use: ```bash npm install --global rea-agents rea --help ``` For native analysis, configure a provider first. See the [CLI and Evidence guide](docs/cli.md) for native commands, provider selection, snapshots and scripting. ### Update REA REA changes quickly, and new releases include frequent bug fixes. Keep your installation up to date. For a CLI installed with `npm install --global` or `bun add --global`: ```bash rea update ``` `rea --update` is an alias for this verified workflow and accepts the same global output flags. Use `rea update` when combining it with other command controls. Updater commands retain at most 4 MiB of stdout and stderr combined. Oversized metadata replies are rejected after the command exits; verbose installs continue with bounded diagnostics. Human progress output respects terminal backpressure and waits for submitted writes to finish. Bun global updates require Bun 1.2.17 or later. With an older Bun release, upgrade Bun manually before running `rea update`. To refresh your agent registrations and skill, run the setup command printed by the update. If you use `npx`, update your agent setup with: ```bash npx rea-agents@latest setup ``` Review the setup changes and restart your agent. For one-off CLI commands, use `npx rea-agents@latest` followed by the command. With Bun, use `bunx rea-agents@latest` in place of `npx rea-agents@latest`. ## How REA works Your agent calls REA through MCP to inspect the target and trace relevant code. REA returns findings with their evidence. The agent uses them to ask follow-up questions, explain the behavior, or write and test an implementation. CLI commands use the same workflows. ![REA investigation flow: your agent asks about a local target, REA inspects and traces it using analysis tools, and the agent uses the returned code, references and unknowns to explain, implement and test.](website/public/assets/figures/rea-investigation-flow.svg) [Open the full-size figure](website/public/assets/figures/rea-investigation-flow.svg). ## What you can analyze REA requires Node.js 22.x (>=22.23.4), 24.x (>=24.22.1), or 26.12.1+, plus npm. Additional tools and host support depend on the target: | Target | What REA returns | Requirements and guide | | ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Desktop installations | Runtime candidates, supporting files, component markers and next probes | Built-in bounded directory/header inspection; [desktop applications](docs/desktop-applications.md) | | Native binaries | Pseudocode, assembly, strings, symbols, calls and references | Hopper, Ghidra, IDA or Kuna; [native analysis](docs/native-investigation.md) | | Offline ELF layout | Sections, segments, original symbols/relocations and static mitigation candidates | Caller-supplied pwntools on Linux x64; [binary diagnostics](docs/binary-diagnostics.md) | | Go binaries | Embedded compiler version, modules, replacements and build settings | Built-in static ELF/PE/thin Mach-O inspection; no Go installation required | | GPU code objects | CUDA/HIP targets, selected kernel parameters and resources, retained PTX text | Built-in static ELF/PE/fatbin/CUBIN/PTX inspection; [GPU code objects](docs/gpu-code-objects.md) | | Model artifacts | GGUF / safetensors metadata, tensor declarations and derived totals | Built-in header inspection; optional full-file hash; [model files](docs/model-artifacts.md) | | IL2CPP metadata | Unity global-metadata.dat assembly images, type and method names and index ranges | Built-in static decoding of versions 24, 27, 29, 31 and 39; no Unity required | | Godot PCK | Archive inventory and extraction, original header/directory facts and selected content identities | Built-in static formats 2, 3 and 4; no Godot required | | Rust binaries | Embedded cargo-auditable crate names, versions, sources and dependency edges | Built-in static ELF/PE/thin Mach-O inspection; [Rust binaries](docs/rust-binaries.md) | | PE certificates | Authenticode WIN_CERTIFICATE entries and PKCS#7 signer/X.509 identity fields | Built-in static PE inspection; [PE certificates](docs/pe-certificates.md) | | PE imports | Import and delay-load DLL names, ordinals, IAT RVAs and pefile import hash | Built-in static PE inspection; [PE imports](docs/pe-imports.md) | | ELF notes | PT_NOTE/SHT_NOTE owners, types, GNU build-id and ABI-tag fields | Built-in static ELF inspection; [ELF notes](docs/elf-notes.md) | | Binary hardening | PIE, NX, RELRO, CFG and related header flags for ELF, PE and Mach-O | Built-in static header inspection; [binary hardening](docs/binary-hardening.md) | | Apple IPS crashes | .ips metadata, threads, images, registers and documented crash classes | Built-in static JSON inspection; [Apple IPS](docs/apple-ips.md) | | Linux kernel modules | .modinfo keys, __versions CRCs, this_module presence, and signature trailer | Built-in static ELF inspection; [kernel modules](docs/kernel-modules.md) | | Erlang BEAM | IFF chunks, atoms, exports, imports, lambdas and the Code header | Built-in static BEAM inspection; [Erlang BEAM](docs/erlang-beam.md) | | WASM artifact | Validation, sections, exact import/export WAT forms and decoded WAT | Caller-supplied WABT 1.0.42; `inspect_wasm_artifact` | | EVM bytecode | Dispatch selectors, byte offsets, inferred arguments and mutability | Local raw/hex carrier on Linux x64; [offline EVM guide](docs/evm-bytecode.md) | | SQLite databases | Tables, columns, indexes, views, triggers and selected ordinary-table rows | Local database/WAL snapshot; Node.js 24.x >=24.15 or 26+ with native SQLite limits | | Recorded Linux crashes | Raw notes, every recorded thread's registers/signals and optional mapping candidates | Caller-supplied pwntools on Linux x64; optional GDB/pwndbg; [recorded crashes](docs/recorded-crashes.md) | | JavaScript / Electron | Modules, imports, source maps, routes, IPC and native add-on relationships | Node.js and npm; Linux: procps-compatible `ps`; [application analysis](docs/javascript-application-workflows.md) | | Websites | Page structure, scripts, network observations and requested screenshots | A Chrome-family browser; [browser analysis](docs/browser-observation.md) | | Saved network captures | Requests, responses, exposed payloads and source locations | HAR or Fiddler Everywhere SAZ; mitmdump on Linux for native mitmproxy; [capture guide](docs/web-network-captures.md) | | .NET assemblies | Metadata, CIL instructions, declared native dependencies and build comparisons | None (static only); [managed-code guide](docs/managed-code-analysis.md) | | Android APKs | Manifest declarations, classes, decompiled methods and references | Headless JADX and a full JDK on Linux/macOS/Windows x64; [Android guide](docs/android-analysis.md) | | APK signatures | v1/v2/v3/v3.1 signers, certificate fingerprints, key rotation and digest self-consistency | None (static only); `inspect_apk_signature` | | Android devices | Devices, packages, processes, logs, dumps, screen captures, and APK/file transfers | Caller-supplied adb (emulator or hardware); [ADB guide](docs/adb-device-analysis.md) | | JEB projects | Engine-backed project units, artifact digests and type/method pseudo-code | A caller-started JEB client serving MCP, selected with REA_JEB_MCP_URL; [JEB guide](docs/jeb-analysis.md) | | Android resources | Decoded manifest, string tables, locales and version facts | Caller-supplied Apktool launcher; [resource guide](docs/apktool-resource-analysis.md) | | Flutter apps | Dart snapshot hash, per-ABI library digests and engine build provenance | None (static APK parsing); [Flutter guide](docs/flutter-analysis.md) | | Firmware | Regions, extraction results and native-analysis handoffs | Binwalk / Unblob on Linux; [firmware guide](docs/firmware-analysis.md) | | Recorded packets | Selected fields, repeated values, filters and decode-as rules | Linux: TShark 4.x + prlimit; [capture guide](docs/packet-captures.md) | | Packet summaries | Endpoints, DNS, TLS SNI, protocol distribution and HTTP requests | Caller-supplied tshark and capinfos (Linux-verified); [pcap guide](docs/pcap-analysis.md) | | Recorded logic signals | Decoder annotations, sample ranges and diagnostics | Linux: sigrok-cli 0.7.2 + prlimit; [signal recordings](docs/signal-recordings.md) | | Packages and resources | File inventories, digests, plists, Apple bundle anatomy and extracted resources | [Artifact and JavaScript guide](docs/javascript-artifact-reconstruction.md), [Apple applications](docs/apple-application-analysis.md) | | Process behavior | Terminal output, interactions, exit and filesystem observations, and run comparisons | Linux/macOS with a native PTY; [process capture](docs/process-capture.md) | | PyInstaller executables | CArchive members, Python version, entry scripts and extracted bytecode | None (static only); [Python packaged applications](docs/python-packaged-applications.md) | Static JavaScript and .NET inspection read the supplied files without running the application. Runtime capture runs or interacts with the selected target using your user permissions; each runtime guide describes its effects. For offline native-binary inspection, REA also supports caller-supplied GNU objdump and Rizin. See the [reverse-engineering tools guide](docs/reverse-engineering-tools.md) for provider setup, CLI commands, and Evidence limitations. REA does not install or update either provider. Native formats and host support vary by provider. See [Hopper and Ghidra setup](docs/installation.md#hopper), the [IDA guide](docs/ida-provider.md) (including an optional native MCP bridge), the [Kuna decompiler guide](docs/kuna-provider.md), and [experimental Windows Ghidra support](docs/windows-ghidra-p0.md). Ghidra also supports [16-bit DOS analysis](docs/ghidra-dos.md). For large binaries, raise the provider's startup deadline with `REA_GHIDRA_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_MS` or `REA_HOPPER_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_MS`. For provider selection, see the [CLI guide](docs/cli.md#choose-a-provider). Check [release availability](docs/installation.md#released-package-and-main) for features added since the latest npm release. ## Showcases ### DX-Ball: reconstruct a sound-pan calculation Follow a sound call into its position-to-pan helper, inspect the instructions, and turn incomplete pseudocode into C. The reconstruction passes 3,205 original-x86 cases and reproduces all 63 compiled function bytes. [Read the case study](https://rea.tools/showcase/dx-ball/) · [Reconstruction repository](https://github.com/N0zoM1z0/dx-ball) ### Notion: trace the Electron clipboard bridge Find the renderer's clipboard API, follow it through preload and IPC into the main process, and inspect the rich clipboard format. [Read the case study](https://rea.tools/showcase/notion/) ### TH04: recover a DOS bullet-ring calculation Inspect the original PC-98 game's 16-bit instructions, recover the fixed and aimed angle calculations, and compare the reconstructed C++ with the historical compiler output. [Read the case study](https://rea.tools/showcase/th04/) · [Reconstruction repository](https://github.com/N0zoM1z0/th04) ### Build RL environments with REA Record a web app session, turn its API into tools, and export an environment an AI agent can use. Run it with AgentEnv, then add tasks and reward checks for RL training or evaluation. [Read the guide](https://rea.tools/guides/rl-environments/) · [Watch the video](https://x.com/reatools/status/2112574822584918075?s=20) If you've used REA on something interesting, we'd love to see it. Share your case in an [issue](https://github.com/morluto/rea/issues) or a [pull request](https://github.com/morluto/rea/pulls), including the target, your question, how REA helped, and what you found. ## Build RL environments Give an AI agent a local environment to practice tasks such as finding an issue or creating a folder, without running the original app. Use it for reinforcement learning (RL) or to test how well an agent completes tasks. REA turns recorded API requests and responses into tools the agent can call. The environment uses the recorded data and supports changes only when the recording confirms their effects. With REA set up in your agent, replace the example URL and folder tasks below with your own: ```text Use REA to build an RL environment from my test web app at http://127.0.0.1:3000. Cover listing, creating, renaming, and deleting folders. You may create and remove test folders. Leave existing data unchanged. Save it in a folder named my-env. Check which operations work and tell me how to run it. ```
Use the command line instead Use these commands if you already have a file containing the app’s recorded browser requests and responses. Running the result also requires AgentEnv and Docker. ```sh rea environment-build ./session.har ./my-env --name my-env --json agent-env run ./my-env ```
REA exports a runnable environment with a basic test to check that it starts and responds. Use it with your RL framework to define task goals, add reward checks, and run training. [Build an environment](https://rea.tools/guides/rl-environments/) · [Environment reference](docs/agent-environments.md) · [Watch the demo on X](https://x.com/reatools/status/2112574822584918075?s=20) ## FAQ
Which agents can use REA? Any agent that supports local MCP servers. Setup configures the [supported agents](docs/installation.md#supported-agents); other clients can use [manual MCP registration](docs/installation.md#mcp-registry).

items.description: A coding-agent skill for multi-phase security audits with independently verified, machine-readable findings
items.readme_text:
# security-audit

A coding-agent skill that turns your agent into a security auditor. It orchestrates isolated agents through reconnaissance, coverage-led hunting, candidate validation, structured output, independent record verification, and target-neutral reporting.

This is the skill that seeded Cloudflare's vulnerability discovery harness, described in [Build your own vulnerability harness](https://blog.cloudflare.com/build-your-own-vulnerability-harness). The harness grew into a multi-stage, fleet-wide system; this skill is the single-repo starting point it evolved from.

## What it does

The skill runs a structured audit in six phases:

1. **Reconnaissance** -- map architecture, trust boundaries, input surfaces, prior evidence, and deterministic coverage in `architecture.md` and `coverage-ledger.json`.
2. **Coverage-led hunting** -- assign isolated hunters from ledger units, record their checks, and use coverage critics to find gaps.
3. **Candidate validation** -- give every unique candidate to a fresh verifier that tries to disprove it.
4. **Structured output** -- write `confirmed`, `needs_validation`, and `rejected` records to `findings.json` and validate them against `report-schema.json`.
5. **Independent record verification** -- fresh agents verify final source claims. Material replacements receive another independent verifier.
6. **Target-neutral reporting** -- derive `REPORT.md`, `FINDINGS-DETAIL.md`, and `NEEDS-VALIDATION.md` from the verified records and coverage ledger.

The parent runs `validate-coverage-ledger.cjs` after creating the ledger and after each later ledger update. It runs `validate-findings.cjs` in Phase 4 and again after every Phase 5 replacement.

The verdicts are distinct: `confirmed` has a complete source trace and bounded observed result, `needs_validation` has an exact unresolved fact and no severity, and `rejected` records a disproved candidate.

Multiple runs against the same repo are additive. The skill uses prior ledgers and findings to target gaps, revalidate changed source, and carry forward current-source evidence without treating stale or unresolved work as covered.

## Files

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `SKILL.md` | Setup, core principles, platform terminology, workflow overview, and audit anti-patterns |
| `RECONNAISSANCE.md` | Phase 1 reconnaissance prompts and synthesis instructions |
| `HUNTING.md` | Phase 2 orchestration, hunting methodology, and validation rules |
| `ATTACK-CLASSES.md` | Core, wildcard, and obvious-things attack prompts |
| `MEMORY-SAFETY-AND-BINARY.md` | Memory-safety, binary, and kernel hunting classes for native targets |
| `AI-AND-LLM.md` | Prompt-injection, agent/tool, and output-handling hunting classes for LLM-backed targets |
| `WEB-PROTOCOL-AND-AUTH.md` | HTTP request-framing, cache, and authentication-protocol hunting classes for HTTP-protocol and auth targets |
| `CLIENT-SIDE.md` | DOM-injection, messaging-trust, UI-redress, and prototype-pollution hunting classes for client-side/browser targets |
| `SUPPLY-CHAIN-AND-RELEASE.md` | Dependency, CI, release, signing, update, plugin, and extension hunting classes |
| `CLOUD-AND-DEPLOYMENT.md` | IAM, infrastructure-as-code, container, serverless, ingress, and runtime-configuration hunting classes |
| `PROTOCOLS-RPC-AND-MESSAGING.md` | RPC, serialization, queue, broker, webhook, and streaming-protocol hunting classes |
| `RESOURCE-EXHAUSTION-AND-AVAILABILITY.md` | Shared resource, quota, queue, worker, and operator-spend hunting classes |
| `DATA-ISOLATION-AND-LIFECYCLE.md` | Tenant isolation, cache, search, export, backup, migration, deletion, and restore hunting classes |
| `DESKTOP-MOBILE-AND-LOCAL-IPC.md` | Native app, deep-link, webview, exported-component, helper, daemon, and local-IPC hunting classes |
| `VALIDATION-AND-REPORTING.md` | Phases 3–6 candidate validation, structured output, record verification, and reporting |
| `report-schema.json` | JSON schema for all three `findings.json` verdicts |
| `validate-findings.cjs` | Zero-dependency validator for `findings.json` in Phases 4 and 5 |
| `validate-findings.test.cjs` | Findings-validator tests and producer-compatible fixture checks |
| `validate-coverage-ledger.cjs` | Zero-dependency validator for `coverage-ledger.json` in Phases 1–5 |
| `validate-coverage-ledger.test.cjs` | Coverage-ledger validator tests |

## Installation

Install the skill with the [Skills CLI](https://skills.sh):

```bash
npx skills add https://github.com/cloudflare/security-audit-skill \
  --skill security-audit
```

Use `--global` for a user-level installation:

```bash
npx skills add https://github.com/cloudflare/security-audit-skill \
  --skill security-audit \
  --global
```

Run `npx skills --help` for agent-selection and non-interactive options.

## Usage

Start your coding agent in (or pointed at) the codebase you want to audit, then ask it to do a security audit:

```
security audit this codebase
```

```
find security vulnerabilities in ./src
```

```
do a security review, output to ~/audits/my-project
```

The skill activates automatically when the request matches its trigger (security audit, find vulnerabilities, pen-test the code, etc.). A direct codebase audit or pen-test request uses full audit mode. Security questions and focused vulnerability work use guidance mode unless you request report artifacts. In full audit mode, an unspecified output directory defaults to `~/security-audit-skill/<repo-name>/run-<N>`. The workflow writes inside the target repository only when you explicitly select a directory that version control ignores.

## Requirements

- A coding agent with a model that supports tool use and parallel sub-agents
- Node.js for the zero-dependency findings and coverage-ledger validators
- An OS-enforced sandbox for target-controlled builds, tests, processes, browsers, emulators, fuzzers, and fixtures. It must disable external networking, use a sanitized allowlisted environment, enforce resource limits, and allow writes only to assigned scratch paths. Without these controls, the workflow keeps the lead as `needs_validation` instead of executing target code.

## Design principles

- **Only confirm established boundary failures.** Keep a source-grounded blocked lead as `needs_validation` with its exact unresolved fact.
- **Adversarial validation.** The agent that checks a finding is never the agent that found it.
- **Severity requires impact.** Likelihood x impact, not deviation from a checklist.
- **Defense-in-depth gaps are not vulnerabilities.** If Layer A prevents the attack, the absence of Layer B is a hardening note.
- **Multiple runs improve coverage.** In our test runs, a single run found roughly half of the vulnerabilities that repeated runs found in total.

## Contact

Questions, feedback, or comparing notes on AI-driven security tooling: security-ai-research@cloudflare.com

简体中文 · English

DeepSeek Harness 的 Android 客户端。手机上直接跑，也能遥控你电脑上的 DSH。


Trendshift 全语言日榜 #1 · 2026-10-30


Deepy 和鲸娘，陪你干活

干活时敲代码，做完来个空翻，等你确认会举手。打开「App 外显示」，它们还会跟你到桌面。


下载 DSH Go

从 GitHub Releases 或官网下载页获取最新版 APK，常见手机选 arm64 包。

 

感谢大家对 DSH Go 的支持和喜爱，我将尽快适配 iOS 和鸿蒙！大家 Star 点得越多，我适配得越快哦 hhh

第一次用可以先看使用指南，遇到问题欢迎来论坛和 QQ 群。
手机上装过签名不同的早期测试包时不能直接覆盖安装，需要先卸载旧版；卸载会清空对话、Linux 环境和设置。


本机运行，也能遥控电脑

内置 Linux 环境，免 Root、免 Termux。电脑上的 DSH，也能一键切过去接着用。


插话、打断，过程自动收好

回复中途也能插话，排队的消息随时「立即发送」。做完的过程折叠成一行。


原生界面，也有网页版

和官方网页版一键切换，停在同一段对话，下次打开还是你上次用的那个。


分享卡、对话回放和链接

回复一键做成分享卡。整段对话生成链接，对方在浏览器里回放，链接端到端加密。


横屏与平板

横屏手机和平板重新排版：侧栏常驻，内容居中，弹出键盘也不挤。


主题配色与桌面图标

六套主题色，也能跟随壁纸或自选颜色。四款桌面图标，三种功能图标风格。


中文，也说 English

全部界面支持英文，在设置里切换，默认跟随系统。


手机操控

看屏幕、帮你点，三档确认随你选。敏感操作默认交还给你；放宽应用规则或解除限制前，请先了解风险。


## 可以做什么 DSH Go 提供聊天界面、本机运行环境和远程连接，是基于 [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) 的第三方项目。运行在手机上的是 DSH 引擎；模型请求仍由你配置的模型提供方处理。 - **本机运行**：在 App 内安装 Ubuntu、Node.js 与 DSH 运行环境，无需 Root 或另装 Termux。 - **远程连接**：通过 SSH 或李国宝老师开发的 [DSHarness Remote](https://github.com/liguobao/ds-harness-remote) 使用电脑、服务器上的 DSH。 - **聊天与工具**：切换模型，发送图片、使用语音输入，处理工具审批和提问；支持聊天界面与网页模式。 - **插件界面**：使用适配 DSH Go 的原生工具卡、表单和面板；仓库提供 SDK、教程和示例。 - **手机操控**：在你开启权限后，让本机引擎读取屏幕、点按和输入，并可随时停止。 - **分享与外观**：分享、导出和回放对话，调整主题、图标和桌宠。 功能随主机和连接方式不同。DSHarness Remote 当前只支持图片附件，不能在 App 内打开网页版，插件管理限于开关，且不支持 DS Bot 和对话日志导出。详见[本机引擎与远程主机](docs/guide/zh/03-engine-hosts.md)。 ## 安装 安装要求为 Android 8.0（API 26）及以上。Release 页面上的 **arm64** 安装包适用于常见的 64 位 Android 手机；x86_64 设备和模拟器用的 x64 包在发布说明末尾的「其他版本下载」里。仓库没有 32 位 ARM 构建。 1. 从 [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-go/releases/latest) 或[官网下载页](https://go.dshtui.com/download)下载对应架构的 APK，并按系统提示允许该安装来源。 2. 首次启动时，选择在本机安装运行环境，或连接远程主机。 3. 为所选主机配置模型和所需凭据，再开始对话；部分远程渠道需要在主机侧配置。 仅连接远程主机时，不必在手机上安装本机运行环境。手机操控只对正常模式下的本机引擎开放，需要按界面说明开启无障碍等权限；不打扰模式另外要求 Android 14 及以上，以及 Shizuku 或自连 ADB。首次使用可按[使用指南](docs/guide/README.md)逐项配置。 本地引擎默认使用 PRoot 兼容启动。开发者选项中的直接启动默认关闭，开启后的兼容性和回退方式见[常见问题](docs/guide/zh/11-faq.md)。当前 Android 构建以 APK 侧载为目标，不是 Google Play 发布配置。 ## 数据与权限 模型请求会发送给你配置的提供方。开启手机操控后，任务需要的屏幕文字可能发送给模型，支持看图的模型也可能收到截图；请先阅读 App 的权限说明。 “发送匿名使用统计”默认开启，可在首次引导或“设置 → 隐私与分享”关闭。采集范围和关闭后的处理见[常见问题](docs/guide/zh/11-faq.md)。分享内容前，请检查预览；收到链接或文件的人可以保存其中的内容。 ## 风险提示与免责声明 DSH Go 是社区开发的非官方项目，与 DeepSeek 无关联，也不代表 DeepSeek。使用前请了解： - **AI 并非万无一失**：回答、代码和操作可能出错，也可能被网页、消息或文件中的恶意指令误导。请核验重要结果；医疗、法律、投资等高风险决策不应仅依赖 AI 输出。 - **工具会产生真实影响**：本机或远程主机上的命令、文件修改及手机操控可能导致数据丢失、隐私泄露、账号、资金或设备损失。免确认、放宽应用规则或解除限制会减少保护；确认与拦截机制不能保证消除所有风险。建议保留默认保护，只授予必要权限，不在存有支付或银行信息的设备上解除限制。详见[手机操控指南](docs/guide/zh/04-phone-control.md)。 - **第三方服务与费用**：模型、远程主机和插件等按各自条款运行；相关数据处理、服务可用性和费用取决于你选择的服务与配置。本机运行不等于模型离线，也不代表数据不会离开设备。 - **使用前做好防护**：备份重要数据，只连接可信主机、安装可信插件，留意模型用量与费用；不要让 AI 无人值守地处理不可逆或高风险任务。 - **无担保与责任范围**：在适用法律允许的范围内，本软件按“现状”提供，不保证准确性、持续可用性或满足特定用途；相关无担保及责任限制见 [LICENSE](LICENSE) 第 15–17 条。本声明不排除或限制依法不得排除或限制的责任，也不减损你依法享有的权利。 ## 常见问题
和 DeepSeek 官方是什么关系？
没有关系。DSH Go 是社区开发的非官方客户端，基于开源的 [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) 构建。手机上运行的是 DSH 本身；模型请求发给你配置的模型提供方，需要联网，按你在提供方的账户计费。
安全吗？
本机网页版只接受 App 自己的访问。分享链接端到端加密，密钥只在链接里，服务器看不到内容，但获得完整链接的人可以读取并保存内容。手机操控默认保留敏感操作保护；放宽应用规则或开启「解除限制」会减少这些保护。安全机制不能保证零风险，详见[风险提示与免责声明](#风险提示与免责声明)和[手机操控指南](docs/guide/zh/04-phone-control.md)。
切到后台会被杀吗？
部分系统的省电策略会拦住后台。DSH Go 发现后会提醒你，并直达对应的放行设置，vivo、小米、华为、荣耀、OPPO 都有。
对手机有什么要求？
Android 8 及以上。手机直接下载 Release 页面上的安装包即可，模拟器用的 x86_64 版在发布说明末尾的「其他版本下载」里。在手机上运行 DSH 要先准备内置的运行环境，请预留约 1 GB 空间；只连电脑或服务器上的 DSH 可以不装。

# rea-video Reverse-engineer any video. Talking-head, tabletop, AI video, 3D, motion graphics, mixed edits: give it any of them,
and it tells you shot by shot how the visuals, styled text, editing and audio were made, then gives you a plan to make one yourself. [中文](i18n/README_zh.md) | English | [Русский](i18n/README_ru.md) | [日本語](i18n/README_ja.md) | [한국어](i18n/README_ko.md) | [Español](i18n/README_es.md) | [Português](i18n/README_pt.md) | [Français](i18n/README_fr.md) | [Deutsch](i18n/README_de.md) [![Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/JuneYaooo/rea-video?style=flat)](https://github.com/JuneYaooo/rea-video/stargazers) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-%E2%89%A53.10-blue) ![Agent](https://img.shields.io/badge/runs%20in-Claude%20Code%20%7C%20Codex-8A2BE2) Left: a TikTok ad shot on a phone. Right: someone's AI remake with a different product swapped in.
rea-video's verdict: the left is all live footage, one set and two camera positions; the right is all AI-generated, and its 8 shots can be produced in 3 generations.
> Reports come out in the language you ask in (Chinese or English; your agent passes `--lang`). The detailed docs are in Chinese for now; your agent reads them and answers in your language. The six example reports below are in English, so you can see what a report looks like without installing anything. ## What it can break down | Video type | Examples | What you get | |---|---|---| | Live footage | Talking-head, tabletop, handheld product demo, vlog, store visit | Setups and camera positions, framing, camera moves, lighting (12 setups with gear lists), color grade | | AI video | Text/image-to-video, AI short drama, AI music video | Evidence, a reverse-engineered prompt per shot, how to batch into generations and which model to use | | Avatar | A portrait driven by audio, lip-sync | Which shots are avatar shots, what portrait and audio you need | | 3D / animation | Blender / C4D explainers, product animation, 2D animation, stop-motion | Whether to generate with a video model or render from 3D code | | Code / template | Kinetic type, UI demos, charts, slide-style cards | Text, layout and motion timing, ready to rebuild as a Remotion project | | Screen recording | Software tutorials, web demos | Which parts are real material you'll need to record yourself | | Mixed / edits | AI characters + code UI + real screen capture; live footage with AI edits | Each shot judged separately, then reassembled on the original timeline | Besides how the picture was made, every video also gets: - Captions and styled text: start and end of each line (exports to SRT / ASS), plus color, outline and how the text comes in - Stickers, emoji, picture-in-picture: where they sit and how long they stay - Editing: where the cuts are, how fast, whether they hit the beat - Audio: human or AI voice, AI or library music and its BPM, where each sound effect lands - Material you'll supply yourself: screen recordings, screenshots, product photos ## Quick start rea-video is built for AI agents. In Claude Code, Codex or any agent that can run commands, say: ```text Install https://github.com/JuneYaooo/rea-video, then break down this video: /path/to/video.mp4 ``` The agent installs the CLI, learns the workflow and runs the whole thing. You need ffmpeg and Python 3.10+.
Install by hand ```bash brew install ffmpeg # or: sudo apt install ffmpeg git clone https://github.com/JuneYaooo/rea-video && cd rea-video bash scripts/install_skill.sh # installs the CLI (pip, or pipx / a local .venv if pip is blocked) and links the skill into ~/.claude, ~/.codex, ~/.agents rea-video --help ```
You get: - a one-line summary, e.g. "41% AI video + 59% code UI, 8 s of real screen recording, library music at 122 BPM" - a remake plan, split into what to film, what to generate and what to code - a full `report.html` with per-shot frames, evidence, prompts, camera and lighting notes, and the audio breakdown Add a video-capable model — Gemini or Doubao both work: give the agent the endpoint and key. It makes live/AI/3D calls more accurate and writes a reverse-engineered prompt for every shot. Without one it still works; if your agent can see images, it will check the uncertain shots itself. ## Examples

Mixed-media clip · 19 s · 10 shots
AI characters talking + code-built UI + 8 s of real screen recording. The 5 dialogue shots are split up by UI segments but share one set, so one generation covers them.
Video · Report
3D explainer · 67 s · 21 shots
All 3D, AI narration. Doable as 10 video generations, or have an LLM write Blender / Three.js code.
Video · Report

Product promo · 70 s · 12 shots
83% code-driven motion graphics, 12% screen recording. No video model needed; one Remotion project does it.
Video · Report
AI music video · 165 s · 86 shots
Correctly flags the song as AI-generated (it was made with Suno). The vision model called some shots "live-action drama"; the agent spotted fake Chinese characters on a scroll and ruled them AI.
Video · Report

Live-action unboxing · 72 s · 29 shots
All real footage: an overhead phone rig, one rug, one camera position, no voice-over, room sound plus library BGM. After platform transcoding the offline tool called 35% of it AI; agent review brought it to 97% live-action.
Video · Report
AI + real person hybrid · 58 s · 21 shots
75% real (talking head + filming a phone screen) and 25% AI: the creator fed her own on-camera clip and two product photos to Jimeng to generate a "real-person" product segment. The AI part was caught by the Jimeng watermark and garbled text on the gift box.
Video · Report
## Remakes After rea-video breaks a video down, the remake recipe in [cheap-claude-video](https://github.com/JuneYaooo/cheap-claude-video) generates a new version: camera, motion, pacing and transitions follow the original, only the elements you choose are swapped. These results were generated with a self-hosted MiniMax H3: the original shot is the motion reference, and keyframes with the swapped elements (gpt-image-2) set the look. Below are three remakes that OiiOii showed in its WeChat articles. For each we made two versions: the same swap as OiiOii, and one that also swaps the subject, setting and props. Each GIF plays four versions in sync: original, OiiOii remake, our remake, element-swap version.
Overhead outfit change · 12 s
Same swap: woman → man, three outfits → matching menswear. Element swap: a girl in three historical Hanfu outfits in a Chinese study; the remote becomes a round fan.

HD comparison video (with audio) · same-moment stills
Paper-craft / watercolor animation · 30 s
Same swap: new clay girl as the lead. Element swap: a fox; forest → coral reef, clouds → starry sky, sunset → aurora.

HD comparison video (with audio) · same-moment stills
Handheld product video · 21 s · 11 shots
Same swap: an original new product, English sticker → Chinese caption. Element swap: pink product, kitchen → camping table, new ingredients.

HD comparison video (with audio) · same-moment stills
The HD comparison videos use the original audio. The originals and OiiOii versions come from the articles and are shown for comparison only. ## Accuracy How-it-was-made accuracy, weighted by shot duration: | | Tuning set (15) | Holdout (16) | Re-encoded WeChat videos (10) | |---|---|---|---| | Tools only (offline, free) | 98.3% | 99.6% / 98.9% | 88.6% | | + vision model (Gemini) | — | 99.6% / 99.8% | 99.6% | | + agent visual review | — | 99.6% / 99.8% | 100% | The two holdout numbers are holdout (9 videos) and holdout2 (7 videos). On original files the tools alone are mostly enough. Videos downloaded from platforms have been recompressed, which wipes out the noise evidence, so it takes a vision check to get back above 99%. Real-asset detection is 97–99%, and shot boundaries are all correct. Numbers and how to reproduce them: [eval/RESULTS.md](eval/RESULTS.md). ## How it works ![rea-video pipeline](docs/rea-flow_en.svg) 1. Split: cut the video into shots and separate audio into voice, music and effects. 2. Gather evidence: measure the frames (frame cadence, sensor noise, whether the whole image is panning as one plane, AIGC tags in metadata); look at the images (hands, text, physics); listen (BPM, key, singing vs speech). 3. Decide: hard evidence like AIGC tags and frame cadence outranks "looks like". Conflicts are flagged for the agent to review visually. 4. Plan the remake: batch shots according to what the target video model can actually do, such as max clip length, multi-shot support and how many reference images it takes. ## FAQ
How is this different from one-click remake tools like Hypit? [Hypit](https://github.com/hypit-ai/hypit) takes a reference video and makes a new one: the agent reads frame grids to understand the original, generates footage with the models it supports (Seedance, PixVerse, MiniMax, Wan and others), and renders captions and motion graphics in HTML. It doesn't ask how the original was made. A live-action source goes through the same pipeline; it won't tell you how many cameras were used or how it was lit. What AI video it can match depends on the models it has: no Kling or Veo, and no dedicated avatar or 3D path, and no AI music: you bring your own. It is strongest on talking-head, podcast and interview videos that follow a script, and weaker on music-driven edits, product motion graphics and cinematic shorts. rea-video doesn't render a video. It works out shot by shot whether something was filmed, AI-generated or built in code, then gives a shooting plan, prompts or a code approach for each. For a quick lookalike, Hypit is faster. To understand how the original was made and remake it cheaply, use rea-video. They work fine together.
Do I need a video-capable model? What does it cost? No. Tools-only mode is offline and free, and already accurate on original files. For recompressed platform downloads, add a video-capable model (Gemini or Doubao both work) or use an agent that can see images; you pay whatever that service charges. Automatic video generation (capsule-cinema) does a free dry run first and only calls paid models after you confirm.
Can it remake the whole video automatically? Partly. With [capsule-cinema](https://github.com/JuneYaooo/cheap-claude-video) installed, AI shots are generated and placed back on the original timeline automatically. Live shots you film from the shooting plan; code shots the agent writes as a Remotion project. See [docs/replicate.md](docs/replicate.md).
Can I just repost someone else's video? No. rea-video is for learning a video's structure, pacing and techniques, then remaking it with material you have the rights to. Don't reuse other people's footage, music, characters or likeness. Follow platform rules and local AI-content labeling requirements when you publish.
## Docs - [docs/what-it-detects.md](docs/what-it-detects.md): everything it detects (10 visual types, camera, lighting, grade, audio) - [docs/replicate.md](docs/replicate.md): remaking from the report - [docs/cases.md](docs/cases.md): case details - [docs/decompose.md](docs/decompose.md): detection rules - [docs/cli.md](docs/cli.md): CLI usage and capsule-cinema integration - [rea_video/capabilities/](rea_video/capabilities/README.md): capability tables for video / image / audio models, used to pick models for the remake plan - [eval/RESULTS.md](eval/RESULTS.md): eval results The docs are in Chinese for now. ## Community Questions, breakdowns and remake ideas: [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/JuneYaooo/rea-video/discussions). Chat with us on [Discord](https://discord.gg/dZj8D3GqWT). Chinese speakers can also find us on [linux.do](https://linux.do/). Want a video broken down? Open a [request issue](https://github.com/JuneYaooo/rea-video/issues/new?template=request_breakdown.yml) with the link and we'll publish the result as a case. ## Credits Inspired by [REA (Reverse Engineer Anything)](https://github.com/morluto/rea): trace from what you see back to how it was made, back every claim with evidence, and verify by measurement.

QQ 群：386179533（ai技术交流学习群）
扫码或搜索群号加入群聊，一起交流插件使用心得、反馈问题与分享玩法。

的公共网关](https://kilo.ai)，均直连、不经任何第三方中转。请求由谁处理、数据发往何处，见「上游是哪些源」与「免责声明」。 - **清单跟随上游**——模型集合、上下文长度与能力在每次刷新时向上游重新拉取，插件内不保存静态快照。 - **选择器只广播可用的模型**——上游清单已声明但网关明确拒绝路由的模型（返回 `Model is unavailable`、或 404 找不到该 id）从下拉框移除，仅在设置页保留记录并注明拒因；网关自身故障（5xx）、配额限制（429）、超时与断网不属于对模型的判定，一律保持可达；被地区策略拦截的模型归入 region-limited 分组。整轮探测全部被拒时同样保留，选择器不会为空。 - **公告中心 + 实时推送**——仓库维护者在仓库中编辑 JSON 并推送后，所有已安装实例最迟在一个轮询周期内收到；正文为白名单约束下的 HTML，支持图文排版；`urgent` 级别触发全屏弹窗；可选系统级通知。 - **应用内升级**——设置页一键升级：下载 → SHA-256 校验 → 备份 → 原子替换 → 校验回读 → 热重载，任一步失败自动回滚至上一版本。 - **热重载**——升级与代码变更即时生效，无需重启应用；也可在设置页手动触发，或启用文件监视自动重载。 - **按响应体形状判定流式响应**——网关在高负载下会以 / jitterRatio。将这三项嵌套在 backoff:{} 中， 调度器读到 undefined，于是 undefined \* 2ⁿ = NaN，而持久会话日志会直接拒绝非有限数值—— 一个本可恢复的瞬时故障因此导致整轮对话报废。应返回已解析完毕的扁平策略。 **一次被中断的工具调用会永久污染该会话。** 缺少对应结果的工具调用在重放时，上游返回 400 invalid_request_error，此后该会话中的每一次请求都会失败。本插件在发送前修复配对， 三种线协议共用同一处修复逻辑。 **未在 inject 中声明的服务，属性直读会抛错（与返回 undefined 不同）；而 ctx.get() 在服务 "尚未被 provide 出来"时返回 undefined。** 这两条本轮各自触发过一次问题：将 inject 缩减为仅剩 llm 之后，typeof ctx.interval === 'function' 直接抛出 cannot get property "timer" without inject（ctx.interval 是 timer 服务上的 mixin），插件在所有 composition 中 均不再激活；改用 ctx.get('webServer') 后返回 undefined——原因不在于缺少 web server，而在于插件先于 web 半身加载——导致设置页路由全部未注册。正确做法是 ctx.inject(deps, callback)：为所需服务开启一条独立的 fiber 使其待命， 避免在加载瞬间做一次性判断。 ## 为什么按 body 的形状而不是 Content-Type 读响应 该车道会在高负载下以 200 + application/json 返回完整的 SSE 帧序列。旧实现依赖 header， 于是 await response.text() 将整条流读成字符串、JSON.parse 失败、整轮报废——而该 错误对象携带 status: 200，还会使可用性探测将完全可用的模型判为"不可路由"， 使其在下拉框中消失一轮。当前实现先嗅探首块（≤4 KB）按形状分流，再将已读取的字节 重新注入流中，实时性不受影响；src/http.js 的 sniffBody 为唯一判据。 ## 为什么速度那一栏会显示 — 早期版本曾为一条实际仅 ~40 tok/s 的车道报告出 2 941 tok/s。问题不在网关——直连 读包的探针显示 64 个帧跨越 5.6 秒，确为增量投递——而在于分子与分母度量的不是同一段 时间：一次调用计费 422 个输出 token，其中 291 个是未流出任何帧的 reasoning token， 它们在第一个可见 token 之前即已生成完毕，而窗口起点正是该 token。以整段 以整段 completion 耗时除以答案文本落地所用秒数，无法反映解码速度。 因此当前实现仅在"能够容纳分子的那段时间"内输出速率：windowTokens() 将未流出的 reasoning token 从分子中剔除，decodeWindow() 拒绝过短以至于无法计时的窗口以及不真实的 高速率，看板与模型表均改为 共用该行为。触发条件为：首段仅有非空思考、无正文且无工具调用，且上游在未发送正常 结束帧的情况下直接关闭流；或上游发送了正常 stop 收尾、但同样只有思考而无正文——宿主会将 此类「空停」回合判定为空响应，恢复流程会继续请求一次正文。以下情况不触发恢复：用户取消、 已输出正文或工具调用的正常结束、达到输出上限、明确的上游错误。 插件将已收到的思考作为检查点文本，与原始输入一起发起新请求，要求直接输出整理后的回答。 该机制基于检查点重新发起请求，与上游原生 resume 无关，也不会重放已显示的思考内容。恢复段禁用工具调用；已输出 正文或已开始调用工具的截断回合不执行恢复，以避免内容重复或工具重复执行。 为避免重复长思考，恢复提示要求结论优先、最多 800 词；此为提示层面的约束（非硬性 token 限制），模型可能不遵守。恢复属于降级回答，原始请求中的长篇或逐步分析可能被简化。 每个逻辑回合最多两次物理请求：原始请求加一次恢复。默认总时限 900 秒（15 分钟），恢复段最多 300 秒，且受剩余总时长约束；恢复输出上限 8192 tokens，并继续受用户与模型的上限 约束。首段已知的输出 tokens 会从原始预算中扣除，恢复预算不足 512 tokens 时不发起恢复。 检查点最多
